title: Energy, Work and Power Module 5 Lesson 2: Accelerating Vehicle Slope Work Energy custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A car of mass $1000\text{ kg}$ ascends a slope of length $100\text{ m}$ inclined at an angle $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.05$. Its speed increases from $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the total increase in mechanical energy ($\Delta E_k + \Delta E_p$). Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A van of mass $1500\text{ kg}$ accelerates up a hill of length $80\text{ m}$ inclined at $\alpha$ where $\sin\alpha = 0.04$. The speed increases from $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ against a constant resistance of $500\text{ N}$. Calculate the work done by the van's engine. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A car of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ descends a slope of length $200\text{ m}$ inclined at $3^\circ$ to the horizontal. The speed increases from $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and the constant resistance is $400\text{ N}$. Calculate the work done by the engine. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A cyclist and bicycle of mass $80\text{ kg}$ ascend a hill of length $250\text{ m}$ inclined at $1.5^\circ$ to the horizontal. The cyclist's speed drops from $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the bottom to $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the top. The work done against resistance is $3000\text{ J}$. Find the constant driving force $F$ exerted by the cyclist. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A car of mass $1400\text{ kg}$ enters a slope of length $150\text{ m}$ inclined at $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.05$ with an initial speed of $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Over this distance, the engine does $280\text{ kJ}$ of work and resistance does $75\text{ kJ}$ of work. Find the speed of the car at the top of the slope. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A vehicle of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ coasts up a hill inclined at $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.08$ with its engine switched off. The resistance to motion is a constant $360\text{ N}$. The vehicle decelerates from $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the distance travelled up the hill using work-energy. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.prompt: A car of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ accelerates from a speed of $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ while travelling a distance of $180\text{ m}$ up a hill inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.05$. A constant resistance of $500\text{ N}$ acts on the car. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the increase in kinetic energy of the car, the increase in gravitational potential energy, and the total work done by the engine.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the time taken to travel the $180\text{ m}$ is $12\text{ s}$, calculate the average power developed by the engine in $\text{kW}$.

questions.prompt: A van of mass $2000\text{ kg}$ travels down a straight hill of length $300\text{ m}$ inclined at $2.5^\circ$ to the horizontal. The resistance to motion is constant and equal to $650\text{ N}$. The speed of the van increases from $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ as it travels down the hill. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the increase in kinetic energy of the van and the loss in gravitational potential energy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the work-energy principle to calculate the work done by the van's engine.

questions.prompt: A cyclist and her bicycle have a combined mass of $70\text{ kg}$. The cyclist ascends a straight hill of length $400\text{ m}$ inclined at $2^\circ$ to the horizontal. Her speed at the foot of the hill is $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and her speed at the top is $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The cyclist pedals with a constant driving force of $25\text{ N}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the loss in kinetic energy, the gain in potential energy, and the work done by the cyclist's driving force.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the work-energy principle to find the work done against the resistance forces, and determine the average resistance force opposing the cyclist.

questions.prompt: A train of mass $160000\text{ kg}$ travels up a track inclined at an angle $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.02$. The train's engines work at a constant power of $1200\text{ kW}$. A constant resistance of $16000\text{ N}$ opposes the motion. The train travels a distance of $600\text{ m}$ up the incline in $40\text{ s}$, with its speed increasing from $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total work done by the train's engines during the $40\text{ s}$, the gain in gravitational potential energy, and the work done against resistance over the $600\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Apply the work-energy principle to calculate the increase in kinetic energy of the train, and find its initial speed $u$ to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A test car of mass $1000\text{ kg}$ is driven up a rough straight track inclined at an angle $\alpha$ where $\sin\alpha = 0.1$ and $\cos\alpha = 0.995$. The coefficient of friction between the tyres and track is $\mu = 0.04$, and aerodynamic drag adds a further constant resistance of $200\text{ N}$. The car accelerates from $14\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $22\text{ m s}^{-1}$ over a distance of $120\text{ m}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total resisting force opposing the car and the total work done against resistance over the $120\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the engine and the average driving force exerted by the car over this distance.

questions.prompt: A car of mass $1600\text{ kg}$ is pulling a trailer of mass $800\text{ kg}$ up a straight hill of length $600\text{ m}$ inclined at an angle $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.06$. The resistance to motion is $500\text{ N}$ on the car and $300\text{ N}$ on the trailer. The car and trailer are connected by a light rigid towbar. The speed of the combination decreases from $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the bottom of the hill to $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the top. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use an energy method to calculate the loss in kinetic energy of the system, the gain in potential energy, and the constant driving force $F$ exerted by the car's engine.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the constant acceleration of the system and use it to determine the tension in the towbar between the car and trailer during the ascent.

questions.prompt: An enclosed cable car of mass $4500\text{ kg}$ is launched from the lower terminal of a mountain tramway and hauled up a track inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal by a haul rope parallel to the track. The resistance to motion is constant at $1200\text{ N}$. The car accelerates from rest at the bottom to a cruising speed of $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ over a distance of $80\text{ m}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the increase in kinetic energy of the cable car, the increase in gravitational potential energy, and the total work done by the haul rope over this $80\text{ m}$ launch section.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Assuming constant acceleration during the launch, calculate the tension in the haul rope during acceleration, the time taken for the launch, and the peak power delivered by the haul rope at the instant cruising speed is reached in $\text{kW}$.
